title: Configure Amazon Cognito
content:
Objectives Use Amazon Cognito User Pools to implement registration, login, and logout functionality for CloudManga.
Implementation Steps Step 1: Create a User Pool Access AWS Management Console → Amazon Cognito. Select Create user pool. Configure Email as the login method. Enable email address verification. Complete the User Pool creation process. The User Pool used in the project is named User pool - yowtoa.
Step 2: Configure the App Client In the User Pool, create the CloudManga-Web application with the following settings:
Component Configuration Application type Single-page application (SPA) Authentication Authorization Code Flow with PKCE Callback URL http://localhost:5500/ Production Callback URL https://gggiang4689.github.io/CloudManga/ Sign-out URL Corresponding application URLs Configure Cognito Managed Login to provide the login and account registration interface.
Step 3: Connect the Frontend Update the following information in config.js:
Cognito Domain App Client ID Redirect URI OAuth Scopes The frontend redirects users to Cognito Managed Login when they select the login option. After successful authentication, Cognito redirects users back to the application and provides an authorization code to exchange for tokens.
Figure 5.6.1. CloudManga login interface using Amazon Cognito.

The Access Token is used to authenticate API requests that require user permissions.

title: Configure IAM Role
content:
Objectives Create an IAM Role that allows AWS Lambda to access data stored in Amazon S3 and write logs to Amazon CloudWatch.
Implementation Steps Step 1: Create an IAM Role Access AWS Management Console → IAM → Roles. Select Create role. Under Trusted entity type, select AWS service. Under Use case, select Lambda. Attach the AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole policy to allow Lambda to write logs. Enter the Role name: CloudJourney-Lambda-Role. Select Create role. Step 2: Grant S3 Read Permissions Open the newly created Role and select Add permissions → Create inline policy.
Switch to JSON mode and enter:
{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": [ "s3:GetObject" ], "Resource": [ "arn:aws:s3:::cloudmanga-storage-2026/manga/*", "arn:aws:s3:::cloudmanga-storage-2026/covers/*" ] }, { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": [ "s3:ListBucket" ], "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::cloudmanga-storage-2026", "Condition": { "StringLike": { "s3:prefix": [ "manga/*" ] } } } ] } Enter the Policy name:
CloudManga-S3-ReadPolicy
Select Create policy.
Step 3: Verify Permissions Confirm that the IAM Role has the following permissions:
AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole: Writes logs. CloudManga-S3-ReadPolicy: Reads JSON files, cover images, and manga page lists from S3. Results The IAM Role has been configured to allow Lambda to access the necessary resources according to the Least Privilege principle.

title: Create DynamoDB Table
content:
Objectives Use Amazon DynamoDB to store user ratings and reviews.

Enter the configuration information: Component Value Table name CloudManga-Reviews Partition key mangaId – String Sort key userId – String Capacity mode On-demand Select Create table. Step 2: Verify the Table After the table reaches the Active status, open Explore table items to check the data.
Each record contains the following main information:
mangaId: Manga ID. userId: User ID. rating: Rating from 1 to 5. comment: Review content. updatedAt: Update time, if stored. Figure 5.7.1. CloudManga-Reviews table in Amazon DynamoDB.
Results The CloudManga-Reviews table was successfully created and is ready to store the application’s review data.

title: Workshop Overview
content:
Objectives Introduce the problem, architecture, processing workflow, and deployment results of CloudManga, a manga reading and review web application built using Serverless architecture on Amazon Web Services.
1. Problem and Solution CloudManga was developed to create a web application that allows users to search for manga, view detailed information, read chapters as images, and submit reviews after logging in.
To reduce backend server management, the system adopts Serverless architecture. The frontend is built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and deployed on GitHub Pages. Backend functions are handled through Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda.
Amazon Cognito handles user authentication, while Amazon DynamoDB stores review data.
2. Architecture and Storage The CloudManga system uses the following main components:
GitHub Pages: Deploys the web frontend and serves users over HTTPS. Amazon API Gateway: Provides APIs for communication between the frontend and backend. AWS Lambda: Processes requests to retrieve manga lists, read chapters, and manage reviews. Amazon S3: Stores the manga.json file, cover images, and JPG pages; the Bucket is configured as private. Amazon Cognito: Manages user accounts, login, and authentication tokens. Amazon DynamoDB: Stores user ratings and reviews. AWS IAM: Grants Lambda permission to access AWS resources. Amazon CloudWatch: Records logs and supports monitoring Lambda function activities. Image files in S3 are accessed through Presigned URLs generated by Lambda, reducing the need to make the Bucket publicly accessible.
Figure 5.1. Overall CloudManga architecture diagram on AWS.
3. Processing Workflow Users access the CloudManga frontend on GitHub Pages. The frontend sends a GET /manga request to API Gateway to retrieve the manga list. Lambda reads data from S3 and returns manga information along with Presigned URLs for cover images. When a user selects a chapter, the GET /chapter API invokes Lambda to retrieve the corresponding list of JPG images from S3. When logging in, users are redirected to Amazon Cognito for authentication and token issuance. When submitting a review, API Gateway validates the JWT before Lambda stores the data in DynamoDB. The frontend calls GET /reviews to retrieve and display reviews and ratings. 4. Deployment Scope The Workshop focuses on building a small-scale manga reading application with six manga titles, using AWS Serverless services.
The implemented features include manga listing, searching, detail pages, JPG image reading, Cognito login, and DynamoDB-based reviews. The frontend is deployed on GitHub Pages. The backend consists of three main Lambda functions: CloudManga-GetManga, CloudManga-GetChapter, and CloudManga-Reviews.
During the AWS learning process, services such as EC2, VPC, Docker, ECS, and Application Load Balancer were also practiced in separate labs. However, they are not the main processing components of the current CloudManga Serverless version.
5. Results CloudManga has been deployed on GitHub Pages and connected to AWS services. Testing confirmed the ability to display a list of six manga titles, retrieve cover images from S3, read chapters using JPG images, log in through Cognito, and submit reviews stored in DynamoDB.
The project helped me better understand how to connect AWS services, manage IAM permissions, build APIs, and deploy a web application based on Serverless architecture.

title: Build the Manga Reader
content:
Objectives Build an online manga reading feature by displaying JPG image pages stored in Amazon S3.
Implementation Steps Step 1: Design the Manga Reader Page Use two files:
reader.html: Build the manga reader interface. reader.js: Handle loading and displaying chapter content. The interface is designed to display image pages continuously in a vertical layout.
Step 2: Connect the Chapter Reading API When a chapter is selected, the frontend sends the following request:
GET /chapter?mangaId=1&chapter=1 AWS Lambda retrieves the list of JPG pages from Amazon S3 and generates a Presigned URL for each image.
The frontend receives the list of URLs, then loads and displays the images in order.
Step 3: Test the Functionality Open a manga chapter and check that:
Image pages load successfully. Pages are displayed in the correct order. The interface can be scrolled to read the content. Figure 5.8.2. CloudManga's online manga reading feature.

title: Configure JWT Authorizer
content:
Objectives Use the JWT Authorizer of Amazon API Gateway to protect the review submission API, allowing only requests with a valid Cognito Access Token.
Implementation Steps Step 1: Create a JWT Authorizer Access Amazon API Gateway. Select the CloudManga-API API. Open Authorization → Manage authorizers. Select Create authorizer. Select the JWT type. Configure the following information:
Component Value Name CloudManga-Cognito-Auth Identity source $request.header.Authorization Issuer URL Cognito User Pool URL Audience App Client ID of CloudManga-Web The Issuer URL has the following structure:
https://cognito-idp.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com/<user-pool-id> The User Pool ID and App Client ID values are obtained directly from the Amazon Cognito configuration.
Step 2: Protect the Review Submission API In API Gateway → Routes, select:
POST /reviews
Under Authorization, attach the Authorizer:
CloudManga-Cognito-Auth
The APIs are configured as follows:
API Authentication Required GET /manga No GET /chapter No GET /reviews No POST /reviews JWT Authorizer Figure 5.6.2. JWT Authorizer attached to the POST /reviews API.
Step 3: Test Authentication Test the POST /reviews API in two scenarios:
Without a token: The API rejects the request with the 401 Unauthorized status code. With a valid Access Token: The request is forwarded to AWS Lambda to validate and process the review data. The frontend sends the token in the HTTP Header:
Authorization: Bearer <access-token> Results Completed the JWT Authorizer configuration to protect the POST /reviews API.
The system allows users to view manga lists and reviews publicly but requires login before submitting a review.

title: Create AWS Lambda
content:
Objectives Use AWS Lambda to retrieve data from Amazon S3 and provide manga information to the frontend.
Implementation Steps Step 1: Create a Lambda Function to Retrieve the Manga List Access AWS Console → Lambda → Create function. Select Author from scratch. Enter the Function name: CloudManga-GetManga. Select Python 3.x as the Runtime. Under Execution role, select Use an existing role. Select CloudJourney-Lambda-Role. Click Create function. Step 2: Develop the Processing Function The CloudManga-GetManga function uses the Boto3 library to:
Read the manga/manga.json file from Amazon S3. Convert JSON data into a manga list. Generate Presigned URLs for cover images. Return the results in JSON format for the frontend. Step 3: Create a Lambda Function to Read Chapters Create another Function:
CloudManga-GetChapter
The function performs the following tasks:
Receive two parameters: mangaId and chapter. Use Boto3 to retrieve the corresponding JPG images from S3. Sort the images by filename. Generate a Presigned URL for each page. Return a list of URLs to display on the manga reader page. Step 4: Test Lambda On the Function management page, select Test to verify the returned results.
Figure 5.5.1. Testing the CloudManga AWS Lambda function.
Check the JSON response and confirm that the execution was successful.
Results The CloudManga-GetManga and CloudManga-GetChapter functions have been created to process manga data stored in Amazon S3.
The data is returned in JSON format, including Presigned URLs used to display images.

title: Proposal
content:
First Cloud AI Journey – CloudManga Capstone Project 1. Executive Summary CloudManga is a project aimed at developing a manga reading web application on the Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud computing platform.
The application allows users to browse manga lists, search for manga, view detailed information, and read sample chapters in PDF format. In addition, the system is designed to support user registration, login, and manga reviews.
CloudManga uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript for the frontend, combined with AWS services such as Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon Cognito, and Amazon DynamoDB.
The main objective of the project is to explore how to build a web application using Serverless architecture, reducing the need for server management and taking advantage of AWS managed services.
2. Problem and Solution Problem Online manga reading applications need to manage multiple manga titles, chapters, and user information. Deploying the entire system on traditional servers may require server configuration, operating system maintenance, database management, and resource monitoring. In addition, the application requires a user authentication mechanism to manage interactive features such as manga ratings and reviews. Solution CloudManga uses Serverless architecture to simplify the deployment process:
Amazon S3 stores manga information, cover images, and sample PDF chapters. AWS Lambda processes requests from the application. Amazon API Gateway provides endpoints for the frontend. Amazon Cognito manages user accounts and authentication. Amazon DynamoDB stores ratings and reviews. Amazon CloudWatch supports monitoring Lambda execution. GitHub Pages is used to deploy the static web frontend. The project prioritizes a simple architecture, low costs, and suitability for educational purposes.
3. Solution Architecture Overall CloudManga Architecture The system is divided into three main components:
Frontend: The user interface is built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Backend: Amazon API Gateway works with AWS Lambda to receive and process requests. Storage and Authentication: Amazon S3 stores manga content, DynamoDB stores reviews, and Cognito manages user accounts. The services are connected through APIs to limit direct frontend access to private data.
Request Processing Flow The expected workflow is as follows:
The user accesses the CloudManga website. The frontend sends a request to Amazon API Gateway. API Gateway invokes AWS Lambda to retrieve the manga list. Lambda reads JSON data from Amazon S3. The result is returned to the frontend for display. The user logs in through Amazon Cognito. Authenticated users can submit manga reviews. Lambda stores review information in Amazon DynamoDB. AWS Services Used AWS Service Role Amazon S3 Stores manga data, cover images, and PDF files AWS Lambda Handles application business logic Amazon API Gateway Provides APIs for the frontend Amazon Cognito Handles user registration and authentication Amazon DynamoDB Stores ratings and reviews AWS IAM Manages access permissions Amazon CloudWatch Monitors logs and errors AWS Budgets Controls costs 4. Technical Implementation Main Features Feature Description Homepage Displays the manga list Search Searches for manga by title Manga Details Displays manga information and chapter lists Manga Reader Displays sample PDF chapters Registration and Login Authenticates user accounts through Cognito Manga Ratings Allows ratings from 1 to 5 stars Reviews Allows users to submit and view reviews Planned APIs Method Endpoint Function GET /manga Retrieves the manga list GET /manga/{id} Retrieves manga details GET /manga/{id}/chapters Retrieves the chapter list GET /reviews/{mangaId} Retrieves reviews POST /reviews Adds a review PUT /reviews/{mangaId} Updates a review DELETE /reviews/{mangaId} Deletes a review The GET /manga endpoint has been implemented and tested during the AWS Lambda and API Gateway practice exercises.
The remaining endpoints are within the design scope and will be tested once the implementation is complete.
Data Storage The Amazon S3 Bucket cloudmanga-storage-2026 stores manga data and is configured to block public access.
Reviews are planned to be stored in the DynamoDB table CloudManga-Reviews, using manga IDs and user IDs to distinguish reviews.
The authentication system is planned to use Amazon Cognito User Pool and JWT to protect requests for adding, updating, and deleting reviews.
5. Implementation Roadmap Phase Activities Result 1 Learn about AWS, IAM, VPC, EC2, and S3 LABs completed 2 Create S3, Lambda, and API Gateway Manga list API operational 3 Practice Docker, ECS, ALB, and Auto Scaling LABs completed 4 Develop the CloudManga frontend In progress 5 Integrate Cognito, DynamoDB, and PDF Reader Planned 6 Test, publish, and complete documentation Planned 6. Risks and Limitations The project is carried out within a short period, so basic features are prioritized. The initial manga dataset contains only a small number of titles for testing purposes. Integrating multiple AWS services may cause IAM permission or CORS configuration errors. Some services may incur costs depending on usage. The system has not been tested under heavy loads or evaluated for operation in a real-world production environment. 7. Future Development Add a manga content management dashboard. Support advanced search and genre filtering. Create a favorite manga list. Save manga reading history. Improve the interface on mobile devices. Add more efficient content storage and delivery mechanisms. Explore the use of AI to recommend manga based on user preferences.

title: Integrate Login and Reviews
content:
Objectives Integrate Amazon Cognito and the Reviews API into the CloudManga interface to support login and manga reviews.
Implementation Steps Step 1: Integrate Login Configure Amazon Cognito information in the config.js file.
The login and logout buttons on the interface are linked to Cognito Managed Login.
After successful authentication, the application receives the token and updates the login status.
Step 2: Integrate the Review Feature The reviews.js file performs the following tasks:
Call the GET /reviews API to display the review list and average rating. Display a rating form from 1 to 5 stars. Check the login status before submitting a review. Send a POST /reviews request with the Cognito Access Token. Update the review list after successful submission. Step 3: Test the Functionality Test the login, logout, and review submission features.

title: Project Setup
content:
Objectives Prepare the frontend source code, folder structure, and development environment for the CloudManga application before connecting it to AWS services.
1. Create the Project Folder Create the CloudManga-Capstone folder and open it using Visual Studio Code.
The application’s source code structure:
CloudManga-Capstone/ ├── index.html ├── style.css ├── app.js ├── config.js ├── detail.html ├── detail.js ├── reader.html ├── reader.js └── reviews.js Main components:
index.html / app.js: Homepage, manga list, and search functionality. detail.html / detail.js: Manga details page and chapter list. reader.html / reader.js: Displays manga pages as JPG images. reviews.js: Displays and submits manga reviews. style.css: Interface design. config.js: Configures the API address and Amazon Cognito. 2. Configure AWS Connections The config.js file is used to manage connection information between the frontend and backend.
The main configurations include:
API Gateway Endpoint: API address for handling manga lists, chapters, and reviews. Amazon Cognito Domain: Login page address. Cognito App Client ID: Application identifier. Redirect URI: Redirect address after login or logout. The API endpoint used:
https://oo4qm8mooj.execute-api.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com/manga The configuration information must be updated after completing the setup of Amazon API Gateway and Amazon Cognito.
Sensitive information such as AWS Access Keys or Client Secrets must not be stored in publicly accessible frontend source code.
3. Test the Application on Localhost Open a Terminal in the CloudManga-Capstone folder, then run the following command:
python -m http.server 5500 Access the following address:
http://localhost:5500/ Check that the interface is displayed correctly and that the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files function properly.
Figure 5.3.2. Testing the CloudManga interface on localhost.
At this stage, features requiring data from AWS will only function fully after the backend has been configured.
4. Results Completed the preparation of the CloudManga project structure, frontend files, and local testing environment.
The source code is ready to connect to Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, and other AWS services in the following deployment steps.

title: Workshop
content:
BUILDING THE CLOUDMANGA READING APPLICATION ON AWS Overview In this Workshop, I will build and deploy CloudManga, a manga reading and review web application based on the Serverless architecture of Amazon Web Services (AWS).
The system uses Amazon S3 to store manga information and images, AWS Lambda to process data, Amazon API Gateway to provide APIs, Amazon Cognito to authenticate users, and Amazon DynamoDB to store reviews.
The frontend is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, then deployed on GitHub Pages.
The main features include:
Displaying and searching manga lists. Viewing manga details and chapter lists. Reading manga through JPG image pages stored on Amazon S3. Registering, logging in, and logging out using Amazon Cognito. Rating manga from 1 to 5 stars and writing reviews. Using JWT Authorizer to protect the review submission API. Contents Project Overview Prerequisites Project Setup Amazon S3 Configuration Backend Development Amazon Cognito Authentication DynamoDB Reviews Frontend Development GitHub Pages Deployment System Monitoring Testing Resource Cleanup Deployment Results CloudManga has been deployed on GitHub Pages and connected to AWS services.
Website: CloudManga
Source Code: GitHub Repository

title: System Monitoring
content:
Monitoring Process The CloudManga system uses Amazon CloudWatch to record and monitor the activities of AWS Lambda functions.
The monitoring process is carried out as follows:
Access AWS Management Console → CloudWatch → Log groups. Select the Log Group corresponding to the CloudManga-GetManga, CloudManga-GetChapter, or CloudManga-Reviews function. Open Log streams to check execution history and error messages. Monitor the Invocations, Errors, and Duration metrics in the Monitoring section of Lambda. Check and adjust the configuration when errors are detected during API processing. Figure 5.10.1. Monitoring AWS Lambda activities using Amazon CloudWatch.
Limitations The system currently uses the basic monitoring features of Amazon CloudWatch. An automated alerting system or a dedicated monitoring dashboard has not yet been implemented.
Results Amazon CloudWatch supports checking execution history, detecting errors, and monitoring the performance of AWS Lambda functions, assisting in the operation and testing of CloudManga.

title: Resource Cleanup
content:
Objectives Check and clean up AWS resources that are no longer needed after the practical exercises to optimize costs and manage resources efficiently.
Cleanup Process The steps for checking and cleaning up resources are as follows:
Amazon EC2: Stop or delete Instances that are no longer in use. Amazon ECS: Stop Tasks and Services, and delete test Clusters if they are no longer needed. Elastic Load Balancing: Delete unused Application Load Balancers and Target Groups. EC2 Auto Scaling: Delete Auto Scaling Groups and related resources after completing the practical exercises. Amazon CloudWatch: Check Log Groups and log retention periods. AWS Billing: Check incurred costs in Billing and Cost Management. The resources currently supporting the CloudManga website, including Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon Cognito, and Amazon DynamoDB, are retained to maintain the application’s operation.
Notes Resources must be carefully checked before deletion to avoid affecting the running system.
In particular, deleting an S3 Bucket, DynamoDB Table, or Cognito User Pool may result in data loss and directly affect CloudManga’s functionality.
Additionally, resources that may continue to incur costs, such as NAT Gateway, Elastic IP, Load Balancer, and unused storage resources, should be checked.
Results Resources used for separate practical exercises are reviewed and cleaned up when they are no longer needed.
The main CloudManga services continue to be maintained to keep the website operational while minimizing costs incurred by unused test resources.
